title: Potential XSS via unescaped config strings
reasoning: All three components render config-driven strings (config.whatWeKnow, aboutPoints[].body, intakeTitle, etc.) directly into JSX without sanitization. If config is sourced from user input or external data and contains malicious HTML/script tags, React will render it as text by default (safe), but if config ever gets set via dangerouslySetInnerHTML or the config source is compromised, XSS is possible. This is a moderate risk given the trust boundary 'user-input' in the feature metadata.
recommendation: Confirm config is always sourced from a trusted, server-controlled origin and never derived from user input. Document this assumption. If config could be influenced by user input, apply sanitization (e.g., DOMPurify) before rendering.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests validate input sanitization or config data provenance.
suggestedRegressionTest: Security test ensuring config with <script> tags or event handlers in strings renders safely (React escapes by default, but test to confirm no dangerouslySetInnerHTML path exists).
minimumFixScope: Add documentation comment in each component stating config must be from trusted source. Optionally add runtime sanitization if config provenance is uncertain.
